The harness daemons build with the docker driver on the overlay2 store and have no arm64 emulation, so the test builds linux/amd64 only. Multi-platform bake output is covered by TestAccBuildxP53_multiPlatform on cdnode.

Needs a self-signed TLS registry that already holds team/app:1.0; the harness tlsregistry is empty until TestAccRegistryImageDataInsecureSkipVerify seeds it over HTTPS, which covers insecure_skip_verify.
Needs real ghcr.io credentials; the test removes the provider block and asks Docker Hub for an anonymous pull token instead (as TestAccRegistryTokenEphemeral does).

Needs the live Docker Build Cloud service and Docker Hub credentials (TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live in acceptance.json, same reason); the harness has neither. The test removes both blocks and applies the rest.
Needs a BuildKit daemon reachable from the provider process over TCP with TLS; the harness has none (a docker-container builder's port is only published inside the dind manager).
The dind harness nodes run on a cgroup v2 hierarchy without io.weight, so runc fails to start a container with a block-IO weight; the test comments the argument out. Unit tests cover the update path.

Pushing one variant of a local multi-platform image needs the containerd image store and a registry the node and the provider reach under the same name; cdnode (containerd store) cannot reach the harness registry at 127.0.0.1:12380.

docker_exec, docker_exec_output and attach use hijacked connections, which the moby client dials itself with tls.Dial from the transport's TLS config (client hijack.go), not through the provider's DialTLSContext wrapper (daemonTLSDial). A TLS failure there keeps the client's own text. Covering it needs the moby client to dial hijacks through the transport (upstream) or a wrapper around every hijacking call.

With HTTPS_PROXY set, http.Transport runs the TLS handshake itself after CONNECT and never calls DialTLSContext, so a certificate or handshake failure behind a proxy is not annotated. The Configure preflight still classifies it from the error text; later operations show the raw error.

Under TLS 1.3 the server rejects a missing or bad client certificate after the client's handshake completes, so the alert arrives on the first read, not in daemonTLSDial's Handshake; the moby client rewords it ('check your TLS client certification settings') and the preflight classifies that text, but operations after Configure keep the client's message. A read-side wrapper on the TLS conn (like daemonPlainConn) would cover it; not done in Pass 6c.

buildx:builder: driver = "cloud" (Docker Build Cloud) is tested only against a fake auth server and a fake BuildKit proxy (TestBuildxBuilderCloud, TestBKCloud*), never against the live service. Three behaviours follow buildx v0.38.2 by assumption: the provider dials the builder group at the default proxy build-cloud.docker.com:443 (buildx looks up per-platform instances through the Hub API), sends buildx-version: v0.38.2, and loads results through the build session (buildx's cloud pull is not implemented). The same gap is recorded as acceptance TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live (why the harness cannot run it), partial_marker buildx:builder and example resources/docker_buildx_builder (resource.docker_buildx_builder.cloud and output.cloud_builder); this row is the release note. Close all four when TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live has passed.

compose:cli-config: A compose project with a service build.ssh entry that has a path (id: path, e.g. default: /home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519) loses its whole structured project output on docker_compose and data.docker_compose_config: compose-go v2.16.2 SSHKey.MarshalJSON (types/ssh.go:49-54) writes "id": path, which is not valid JSON as a list element, so json.Marshal(types.Project) fails and composeProjectValue falls back to {"name": ...}. Every other field of project is null and no diagnostic is raised (the value never reaches the outputs contract). compose_yaml is not affected. Fix: marshal SSHKey entries in a fixup before encoding and make a failed encode a diagnostic.
items.reproduce:
data "docker_compose_config" "x" {
  content = <<-YAML
    services:
      app:
        build:
          context: .
          ssh:
            default: /home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519
  YAML
}
output "svc" { value = data.docker_compose_config.x.project.services }

terraform apply: svc is null (project carries only name). The same content in docker_compose gives the same project.

items.reason: compose:services: docker_compose (mode = "local") runs pre_start steps with per_replica: true once for every replica it creates and always removes a step container once it exits; compose v5.7.0 (pkg/compose/pre_start.go:115-147 runPreStart) rejects per_replica: true and keeps a failed step container for inspection. A project that uses per_replica applies with the provider but fails with docker compose up, and after a failed step there is no container left to inspect (the provider's error carries the last 20 log lines of the step).
items.reproduce:
resource "docker_compose" "x" {
  name    = "prestart"
  content = <<-YAML
    services:
      web:
        image: nginx:alpine
        deploy: { replicas: 2 }
        pre_start:
          - command: ["sh", "-c", "exit 0"]
            per_replica: true
  YAML
}

terraform apply succeeds (two step containers run, both removed); docker compose -p prestart up -d with the same YAML fails.

items.reason: compose:services: docker_compose (mode = "local") applies use_api_socket: true by always adding the Engine socket bind mount, DOCKER_CONFIG=/run/secrets/docker (unless the service sets it) and the #apisocket config.json. compose v5.7.0 (apiSocket.go:45-132) adds DOCKER_CONFIG and the config file only when the host has registry credentials and the service does not set DOCKER_CONFIG, with mode 0600. In those two cases the com.docker.compose.config-hash label differs from the CLI's, so a container created by one is recreated by the other. Projects managed only by the provider are not affected.
items.reproduce:
services:
  app:
    image: docker:cli
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    use_api_socket: true
    environment: { DOCKER_CONFIG: /cfg }

docker compose -p apisock up -d with this file, then apply the same content with resource "docker_compose" "x" { name = "apisock" ... }: the plan recreates apisock-app-1 (the same happens with no DOCKER_CONFIG on a host with no registry credentials).

items.reason: engine:registry-image-data: data.docker_registry_image reads config, labels and created from the registry's image config blob with the provider's own registry client, because the daemon's GET /distribution/<name>/json returns no image config. That client falls back to plain HTTP only for localhost and loopback registries (as docker does), so for a plain-HTTP registry on any other host (a daemon insecure-registries entry served over http) the daemon path gives the warning 'Image config not read from registry' and leaves the three values null; digest, platforms and the raw output are still filled. insecure_skip_verify does not help there: it turns TLS verification off but still speaks HTTPS.
